title: 1992 AHSME Problem 29
statement: An “unfair” coin has a \(\frac23\) probability of turning up heads. If this coin is tossed \(50\) times, what is the probability that the total number of heads is even?

solutions.text:
Let \(E_n\) and \(O_n\) be the probabilities of an even and odd number of heads after \(n\) tosses. Then \(E_n+O_n=1,\) while \[ \begin{aligned} E_{n+1}-O_{n+1} &=\left(\frac13-\frac23\right)\\ &\qquad\cdot(E_n-O_n). \end{aligned} \] Since \(E_0-O_0=1,\) we have \(E_{50}-O_{50}=(-\frac{1}{3})^{50}=3^{-50}.\) Solving the sum and difference equations gives \[ E_{50}=\frac12\left(1+\frac1{3^{50}}\right). \]

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Track the difference between the probabilities of an even and an odd number of heads
One toss multiplies that difference by \(P(T)-P(H)\)
